mainTopic: בושת: who can be shamed and why the payment is owed, and רבי יהודה's exclusion of a סומא
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier answer: the minor being discussed is old enough to feel embarrassed. A new משנה then teaches that shaming a naked, blind, or sleeping person makes one liable. A sleeping person who shames someone else is exempt. Someone who falls off a roof pays for damage, but pays for בושת only if he meant to shame. רב פפא explains that the ברייתא's 'naked' person had his clothes blown up by the wind, and that its 'bathhouse' is really a riverbank. רבי אבא בר ממל asks about shaming a sleeping person who dies before waking. רב זביד explains the question as כיסופא (inner feelings) versus זילותא (public disgrace). רב פפא explains it as the victim's own embarrassment versus the family's shame. Each attempted proof from the minor is pushed off: the minor may be old enough to feel shame, and a ברייתא of רבי supports that distinction. Finally, the גמרא shows that the משנה's blind-person case does not follow רבי יהודה, and traces his גזירות שוות for exempting a סומא from בושת, גלות, מיתות בית דין and מלקות.

steps.title: Finishing the answer: a minor who feels embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the earlier answer. The case of the קטן is one where he is old enough to feel embarrassed when people embarrass him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The ברייתא is talking about a minor] who, when people humiliate him, feels humiliated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer. The minor being discussed is old enough to actually feel embarrassment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty was how a קטן can receive בושת at all. The answer limits the case to a קטן who already understands embarrassment. That explains why someone who shames him has to pay.
steps.whatToRemember: The minor in this case gets paid for בושת because he is old enough to feel embarrassed when people shame him.

phrases.english: who, when they humiliate him, feels humiliated.
phrases.notes: This finishes the previous answer. The minor being discussed is old enough to feel embarrassed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous page about a קטן and בושת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minor seems unable to be humiliated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a minor who is mature enough to feel shame.

steps.title: Humiliating a naked, blind, or sleeping person
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who humiliates a naked, blind, or sleeping person is liable. A sleeping person who humiliates someone else is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who humiliates a naked person, a blind person, or a sleeping person is liable. But a sleeping person who humiliates someone is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists victims who are still owed payment for בושת, even though they might not see or feel the shame in the usual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The victim does not need to be dressed, see the person shaming him, or even be awake for liability. What matters on the shamer's side is that he is acting knowingly. That is why a sleeping person who shames someone else is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sleeping cases. Shaming a sleeping person makes you liable, but a sleeping person who shames someone else is exempt.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One who humiliates a naked person,
one who humiliates a blind person,
and one who humiliates a sleeping person — is liable.
But a sleeping person who humiliated someone — is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humiliating a naked, blind, or sleeping person makes one liable. A sleeping person who humiliates is exempt.

steps.title: Falling off a roof: liable for damage, not for humiliation
steps.stepSummary: Someone who falls off a roof and both hurts and embarrasses another person pays for the damage. He does not pay for the humiliation unless he intended it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone fell from a roof and caused damage and humiliation, he is liable for the damage and exempt for the humiliation unless he intended to humiliate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a case where both damage and embarrassment happen by accident. It splits the two payments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזק (damage) is paid even without intent. בושת is only paid when the person meant to embarrass. So one accidental fall gives two different results.
steps.whatToRemember: בושת requires intent; נזק does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic rule about בושת. Intent matters for embarrassment payments in a way it does not for physical damage.

phrases.english: If he fell from the roof,
and caused damage and humiliated —
he is liable for the damage,
and exempt for the humiliation,
unless he intends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accidental falling: pay נזק, but not בושת unless there was intent.

steps.title: A ברייתא: humiliating someone naked or in a bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says one who humiliates a naked person, or someone in a bathhouse, is liable. But that humiliation is worth less than humiliating a clothed person or someone in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: If one humiliated someone naked, he is liable, but it is not the same as humiliating him clothed. If he humiliated him in a bathhouse, he is liable, but it is not the same as humiliating him in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds to the משנה's case of a naked person. It says liability stays, but the amount changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with the משנה that shaming a naked person brings liability. It adds that the payment is smaller, because the setting already makes the shame less. The bathhouse case works the same way.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not comparable' does not mean exempt. He still pays; the amount is just smaller.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
If he humiliated him while naked — he is liable,
but humiliating him naked is not comparable
to humiliating him clothed.
If he humiliated him in the bathhouse — he is liable,
but humiliating him in the bathhouse is not comparable
to humiliating him in the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's naked-person case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaming a naked person or someone in a bathhouse is liable, but it is worth less than in normal settings.

steps.title: Can a naked person even be humiliated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling about a naked person. It then challenges it: a naked person is already exposed, so how can he be humiliated?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he humiliated him naked, he is liable. But is a naked person subject to humiliation?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-quotes one line from the ברייתא in order to challenge it. It asks how shaming a naked person is even possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone already standing naked seems to have no more dignity to lose. So it is hard to see what extra shame the other person caused. This sets up the need to define the case more exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said (quoting a source in order to discuss it)

phrases.english: The Master said: If he humiliated him naked — he is liable.
Is a naked person someone who can be humiliated?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that one who humiliates a naked person is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A naked person is already fully exposed, so it seems no further humiliation can be added.

steps.title: רב פפא: wind lifted the clothes, and he pulled them higher
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'naked' means wind blew up the person's clothes. The other man then lifted them even higher and embarrassed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What does 'naked' mean? A wind came and lifted his clothes, and this person came and raised them higher and humiliated him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining what kind of 'naked' person the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The victim did not choose to be uncovered; the wind partly exposed him. The other man added real shame by exposing him further. That is why he pays, though less, since the person was already partly exposed.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'naked' person is someone exposed by accident (the wind), and the shamer made it worse. That added shame is what he pays for, at a reduced amount.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: What is meant by 'naked'?
That a wind came and lifted up his clothes,
and this one came and raised them higher and humiliated him.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the person who does the humiliating, not the one whose clothes blew up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by defining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Naked' means someone fully undressed, who cannot be shamed further.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Naked' means someone partly exposed by the wind, whom the shamer exposed even more.

steps.title: How can someone be humiliated in a bathhouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling that humiliating someone in a bathhouse makes one liable. It asks how that is possible, since people are undressed there anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he humiliated him in a bathhouse, he is liable. Is a bathhouse a place where a person can be humiliated?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second case in the same ברייתא, a bathhouse. It challenges it the same way it challenged the naked-person case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a bathhouse everyone is undressed, so exposing someone there seems like no shame at all. So how can the ברייתא say he is liable, even for a reduced amount? This is the same question as step 5, now asked about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who can be humiliated; literally, a 'son of shame'

phrases.english: If he humiliated him in a bathhouse, he is liable.
Is a bathhouse a place where one can be humiliated?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 5, now aimed at the ברייתא's bathhouse case
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that humiliating someone in a bathhouse makes one liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where everyone is undressed, exposing a person causes no shame, so there should be no liability

steps.title: רב פפא: it was on a riverbank
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'bathhouse' really means a riverbank where people bathe. Exposing someone there is shameful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case where he humiliated him on the bank of the river.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by changing what case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean a real bathhouse, where no one would be embarrassed. It means a riverbank used for bathing. People there are more careful about covering up, so exposing someone is real humiliation, but less than in the marketplace.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: That he humiliated him
on the bank of the river.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שֶׁבִּיְּישׁוֹ עַל גַּב הַנָּהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about a real bathhouse, where no shame is possible
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a bathing spot on a riverbank, where people still expect some modesty
steps.whatToRemember: Both of the ברייתא's 'low-shame' cases are explained by רב פפא: the 'naked' person had his clothes blown up by the wind, and the 'bathhouse' is really a riverbank.

steps.title: Humiliating a sleeping person who then dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks: if someone humiliated a sleeping person, and that person died without ever waking up, does the humiliator pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל asked: If he humiliated him while he was asleep, and he died, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The victim never woke up, so he never knew he was humiliated. Is there still payment for בושת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה already said that humiliating a sleeping person makes one liable. Here the twist is that the victim dies before waking, so he never feels any embarrassment at all. Is the payment still owed to his heirs?

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question that is not yet decided

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel asked:
If he humiliated him while asleep, and he died, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question building on the משנה's case of a sleeping person
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does one pay בושת for humiliating a sleeping person who dies without ever learning of it?

steps.title: What exactly is the question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason behind רבי אבא בר ממל's question is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his question?
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to know what idea the question really depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not just want the answer. It wants to know why the case is unclear in the first place. That will lead to a basic question about what בושת payment is for.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his question? What is he unsure about?

phrases.english: What is his question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the question in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What idea makes the sleeping-and-died case unclear?

steps.title: רב זביד: is בושת paid for embarrassment or for disgrace?
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains the two sides. If בושת pays for the victim's hurt feelings, a dead man felt nothing. If it pays for lowering his standing, he was still disgraced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said, this is his question: Is it because of embarrassment, and this man died and has no embarrassment? Or maybe it is because of disgrace, and he did disgrace him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד shows that the question depends on what the payment for בושת is really for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ways to understand בושת: כיסופא means the victim's own feeling of shame, and זילותא means the person was lowered in other people's eyes. A man who died asleep never felt כיסופא. But זילותא still happened, because others saw him being disgraced.

keyTerms.meaning: Embarrassment, the victim's own feeling of shame
Disgrace, being lowered in the eyes of others

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד, הָכִי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said, this is his question:
Is it because of embarrassment?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִית לֵיהּ וְלֵית לֵיהּ כִּיסּוּפָא,
phrases.english: And this man died and has no embarrassment.
Or perhaps it is because of disgrace?
And he did disgrace him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד, הָכִי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by naming the idea behind the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question depends on whether בושת pays for כיסופא (inner feelings) or זילותא (public disgrace)
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words. כיסופא is what the victim feels inside. זילותא is what happens to his image in front of others, even if he never knows about it.

steps.title: Proof from רבי מאיר: a minor gets בושת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי מאיר's ruling that a deaf-mute and a minor receive בושת but a שוטה does not. A minor doesn't really feel shame, so the payment must be for זילותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי מאיר says, a deaf-mute and a minor receive payment for humiliation, but a שוטה does not. If you say it is because of disgrace, that is why he teaches 'a minor.' But if you say it is because of embarrassment, can a minor be humiliated?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב זביד's question using a ruling of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young child doesn't understand enough to feel real embarrassment. Yet רבי מאיר says he still receives בושת payment. That only makes sense if בושת is about זילותא, being lowered in front of others.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Meir says:
A deaf-mute and a minor receive payment for humiliation,
a mentally incompetent person does not receive payment for humiliation.
It makes sense if you say it is because of disgrace;
that is why he teaches 'a minor.'
But if you say it is because of embarrassment,
is a minor someone who can be humiliated?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from step 11
steps.raayaObject: That בושת is paid because of זילותא (public disgrace)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's ruling that a minor receives בושת payment

steps.title: But then a שוטה should get paid too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if בושת is about זילותא, a שוטה can also be disgraced, so why does רבי מאיר say he gets nothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? It is because of disgrace? Then even a שוטה should get it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof by pointing to the other half of רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'minor' part of the ruling fits זילותא. But the 'שוטה' part seems to go against it. A שוטה can surely be disgraced in public, so if זילותא is the reason, he should receive בושת too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what? Used to push back on the other side

phrases.english: Rather, what? It is because of disgrace?
Then even a mentally incompetent person should get it too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Threatens the whole proof, because רבי מאיר's ruling seems to not fit זילותא either
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If זילותא is the reason, the ruling that a שוטה gets no בושת makes no sense

steps.title: A שוטה cannot be lowered any further
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a שוטה is already in the most shameful state possible, so humiliating him does not lower him any more. The proof for זילותא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: A שוטה, there is no greater humiliation than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback and saves the proof that בושת is about זילותא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a שוטה is already the lowest standing a person can have, so an insult cannot disgrace him further. So the שוטה getting nothing fits זילותא after all. That clears the way for the גמרא to return to the proof from the minor in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They say, an answer from the Sages

phrases.english: They say: A mentally incompetent person —
there is no greater humiliation than this.
phrases.notes: His condition is already the lowest standing possible, so an insult can't lower him further.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: שׁוֹטֶה – אֵין לְךָ בּוֹשֶׁת גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 13 and keeps the proof of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the problem case (שוטה) actually fits the reason of זילותא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling about a שוטה shows that זילותא can't be the reason for בושת
steps.terutzMaskana: A שוטה cannot be lowered further, so the ruling about him fits זילותא; the proof from the minor is then restated and rejected (steps 15–16)
steps.whatToRemember: The answer removes the problem from the שוטה. A שוטה is already at the lowest standing, so he gets nothing even if בושת is about זילותא. The proof from the minor is not final yet: step 16 pushes it off.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the שוטה ruling does not argue against זילותא. That keeps the proof from the minor alive until step 16 answers it.

steps.title: Back to the proof from the minor
steps.stepSummary: Now that the שוטה question is answered, the גמרא again tries to prove from the minor that בושת is paid for זילותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, let us settle the question from this ברייתא: the payment is for lowering a person's standing. If it were for hurt feelings, can a minor even feel embarrassed?
steps.whatsHappening: The question about the שוטה has been answered. So the גמרא returns to the minor and again tries to settle רבי אבא בר ממל's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small child does not really feel shame. Yet the ברייתא says he gets paid for בושת. So the payment must be for זילותא, which would mean someone who shames a sleeping person who then dies also has to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: let us settle the question from it
being disgraced; having one's standing lowered

phrases.english: In any case, let us resolve from it
phrases.notes: Now that the שוטה question has been answered, the גמרא goes back to the proof from the minor.

phrases.english: that it is because of disgrace,
for if it were because of embarrassment,
is a minor capable of embarrassment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the challenge from the שוטה has been answered, the proof from step 12 is stated again.
steps.raayaObject: That בושת is paid for זילותא, not for כיסופא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא (רבי מאיר): a minor receives בושת

steps.title: The minor is old enough to feel shame
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא is talking about a minor who already feels humiliated when people shame him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said in another place, we are talking about a child who feels humiliated when people humiliate him. Here too, the child in the ברייתא feels humiliated when people humiliate him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The minor in the ברייתא is not a baby. He is old enough to feel embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this child really feels shame, then the ברייתא also fits the כיסופא side. So it proves nothing about זילותא, and רב זביד's version of the question stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every minor gets בושת. It only means the ברייתא can be read as talking about an older child who understands shame, so it cannot serve as proof.

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa said:
where they humiliate him and he feels humiliated,
here too,
where they humiliate him and he feels humiliated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 15 by narrowing which minor the ברייתא means.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the minor feels no shame, but the ברייתא can be talking about a minor who does.

steps.title: רב פפא's way of reading the question
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the question is different: is בושת paid for the victim's own embarrassment, or for the shame of his family?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said this is what רבי אבא בר ממל was asking: is the payment for the person's own embarrassment, and this person is dead? Or perhaps it is for the shame his family feels?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second explanation of רבי אבא בר ממל's question, different from רב זביד's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בושת pays for the victim's own feelings, a dead man feels nothing, so nothing is owed. If it pays for the family's shame, the family is still alive and embarrassed, so the payment would go to them.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he was asking
the shame felt by the family

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a whole new idea: בושת might be about the family's hurt, not only the victim's.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר, הָכִי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: רב פפא said, this is what he was asking:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבא בר ממל, whose question started this whole discussion.

phrases.english: Is it because of his own embarrassment,
and he has died,
or perhaps it is because of the family's shame?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר, הָכִי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב זביד's explanation from step 11 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is whether בושת is for the victim's own embarrassment or for the family's shame.

steps.title: The minor seems to support family shame
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא is brought: since a minor gets בושת even though he feels no shame himself, the payment must be for the family's shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a deaf-mute and a minor get paid for shame, but a שוטה does not. It makes sense if the payment is for the family's shame, because that explains why the minor is included. But if it is for his own embarrassment, can a minor feel shame?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב פפא's version of the question with the same ברייתא of the minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's family is embarrassed when he is shamed, even if he himself does not understand it. So the minor's payment fits best if בושת is for the family's shame.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source is being brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a deaf-mute and a minor receive payment for shame,
a שוטה does not receive payment for shame.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִשּׁוּם בּוֹשֶׁת מִשְׁפָּחָה –
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is because of the family's shame,
that is why it teaches "a minor."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם כִּיסּוּפָא דִידֵיהּ –
phrases.english: But if you say it is because of his own embarrassment,
is a minor capable of shame?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle רב פפא's version of the question from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That בושת is paid for the family's shame
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא (רבי מאיר): a minor receives בושת

steps.title: Then why doesn't a שוטה get paid?
steps.stepSummary: The proof is challenged: if the payment is for the family's shame, a שוטה's family is also embarrassed, so he should get paid too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that it is because of the shame of the family members? Then even a שוטה should get paid too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the family-shame proof using the other half of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה's family is embarrassed when he is shamed, just like a minor's family. So if בושת were for the family's shame, the ברייתא should not say a שוטה gets nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, what?
Is it because of the shame of the family members?
Then even a שוטה too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 18 using the שוטה part of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Questions whether the ברייתא really fits the family-shame side
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The family-shame idea seems to give the wrong result for the שוטה.

steps.title: A שוטה's family shame is already at its peak
steps.stepSummary: The answer: having a שוטה is already the greatest shame. One more insult adds nothing, so no payment is owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שוטה: there is no greater shame than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge about the שוטה, so the proof for family shame stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a שוטה is already the worst shame there is. Shaming him once more does not make it any worse, so there is no new loss to pay for. This matches the answer in step 14, now used for the family-shame side.

keyTerms.meaning: there is nothing; you have no

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד: the question is כיסופא or זילותא. רב פפא: the question is the victim's own embarrassment or the family's shame. The שוטה objection is answered because his shame is already as great as it can be, but the proof from the minor is rejected in step 22.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹטֶה – אֵין לְךָ בּוֹשֶׁת גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ.
phrases.english: A שוטה: you have no greater shame than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹטֶה – אֵין לְךָ בּוֹשֶׁת גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows why the שוטה case is different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The family-shame idea would give a שוטה payment as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שוטה's shame is already as great as it can be. The insult adds no new shame, so nothing is paid.

steps.title: Back to the proof: a minor can't feel shame, so payment must be for the family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and again tries to prove that בושת is paid for the family's shame, since a minor can't feel embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, let's settle it from this: the payment is for the family's shame. If it were for his own embarrassment, can a minor even feel embarrassed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside the side discussion about the שוטה and comes back to its main proof. It says: whatever the answer about a שוטה, the minor case still shows the payment is for the family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a minor gets paid for בושת. A small child doesn't really feel embarrassed. So the payment can't be for his own feelings, and it must be for the family's shame.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us settle the question from it

phrases.english: In any case, let us settle from it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא about a minor receiving בושת, brought back in step 18.

phrases.english: that it is because of the family's shame,
for if it were because of his own embarrassment —
is a minor someone who can feel embarrassment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שוטה problem is answered in step 20, the גמרא goes back to the proof from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That בושת is paid for the family's shame, not the victim's own feelings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that gives בושת to a minor, who supposedly can't feel embarrassed

steps.title: רב פפא: some minors do feel shame
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes off the proof: the ברייתא is talking about a minor who is old enough to feel hurt when shamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Yes, a minor can feel embarrassed. The case is where people shame him and he feels it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question 'can a minor feel shame?' with a plain 'yes'. So the ברייתא doesn't prove that the payment is for the family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that a minor feels nothing. רב פפא says an older child can feel humiliated. The payment could therefore be for his own shame, and the question stays open.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Yes,
where they shame him and he feels shamed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 21 by narrowing the case of the minor.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the question of what בושת pays for is left open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed every minor is unable to feel shame, but an older minor does feel it.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי supports the split between minors
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי says a minor sometimes gets בושת and sometimes doesn't. The גמרא explains this as the difference between a minor who feels shame and one who doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught: רבי says a חרש gets בושת, a שוטה does not, and a minor sometimes does and sometimes doesn't. The first case is a minor who feels shamed when insulted; the second is one who doesn't feel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב פפא. It shows that the הלכה really does depend on whether the minor feels the shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's 'sometimes yes, sometimes no' for a minor is explained by רב פפא's line. A minor who feels the insult gets paid, and one who doesn't feel it gets nothing. This backs up רב פפא's answer that the ברייתא of the minor proves nothing about the family's shame.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it is taught (here it brings support)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'וְהָתַנְיָא' opens a challenge. Here it brings support for רב פפא, like saying 'and so too it is taught.'
steps.whatToRemember: A minor gets בושת only if he is old enough to feel shamed. A שוטה never gets it, and a חרש does.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: Rebbi says:
A deaf-mute — he has payment for shame.
A mentally incompetent person — he has no payment for shame.

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן – פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ לוֹ, פְּעָמִים אֵין לוֹ –
phrases.english: A minor — sometimes he has it, sometimes he does not —
this is where they shame him and he feels shamed,
that is where they shame him and he does not feel shamed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב פפא's distinction from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's distinction between a minor who feels shame and one who doesn't
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי: a minor 'sometimes has, sometimes doesn't have' בושת
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the minor discussion. A minor's right to בושת depends on his ability to feel shamed.

steps.title: The משנה on a blind person does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about shaming a סומא and says it does not follow רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה holds that a סומא has no בושת and is also exempt from גלות, מלקות and court death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who shames a blind person...'. Our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says a blind person has no בושת. In the same way, רבי יהודה exempted a blind person from exile, from lashes, and from court death penalties.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, the case of a סומא. It points out that this line goes against רבי יהודה's opinion, and it quotes his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats a סומא as fully part of the laws of בושת. רבי יהודה takes the blind person out of the laws of בושת altogether. He applies the same exclusion to גלות, מלקות and מיתות בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who must go into exile for killing by accident
Death penalties carried out by the court

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה isn't saying a blind person is less of a person. He holds that the Torah's wording leaves the סומא out of these specific laws.

phrases.english: 'One who shames a blind person,' etc.
Our משנה is not like Rabbi Yehuda;
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A blind person — he has no law of shame,
and so Rabbi Yehuda would exempt him
from being among those liable to exile,
and from being among those liable to lashes,
and from being among those liable to court death penalties.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's line about a blind person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה, who holds that a סומא has no בושת and is exempt from גלות, מלקות and מיתות בית דין.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view about a blind person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that a blind person is left out of these laws. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack. Leaving a blind person out of so many laws needs a basis in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion quoted in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for רבי יהודה's exclusion of a סומא

steps.title: The word 'עינך' links בושת to עדים זוממין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'עינך' in both the בושת passage and the עדים זוממין passage. Blind people can't be witnesses there, so they are left out here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'your eye' from 'your eye' in the passage on עדים זוממין. Just as blind people are not included there, so too blind people are not included here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי יהודה uses a גזירה שוה built on the shared word 'עינך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'לא תחוס עינך' both about בושת and about עדים זוממין. A blind person can't see an event, so he can't be a witness or an עד זומם. The shared word carries that exclusion over to בושת.

keyTerms.meaning: Your eye — the shared word of the גזירה שוה
Plotting witnesses who are proven false
Just as there ... so too here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה leaves a סומא out of בושת through a גזירה שוה of 'עינך'–'עינך' from עדים זוממין, where a blind person can't take part.

phrases.english: He learns 'your eye'–'your eye' from plotting witnesses;
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים: דברים 25:12 (בושת) and דברים 19:21 (עדים זוממין).

phrases.english: just as there, blind people are not included,
phrases.notes: Blind people can't see what happened, so they can't be witnesses at all.

phrases.english: so too here, blind people are not included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'עינך' from עדים זוממין. Blind people are excluded there, so they are excluded from בושת too.

steps.title: The source for exempting a blind person from exile
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה learns from 'בלא ראות' that a סומא does not go to גלות, while רבי מאיר learns from the same words that he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that a blind person is not among those sent to exile? From a ברייתא: 'Without seeing' leaves out a blind person. That is רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר says it comes to include a blind person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next exemption on רבי יהודה's list, which is גלות, and brings a ברייתא as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא gave the source for בושת. Now it gives the source for גלות: the words 'בלא ראות' in the פרשה of accidental killing. The same words are read in two opposite ways. רבי יהודה says they leave out a סומא, and רבי מאיר says they include him.

keyTerms.meaning: People who must go into exile to a city of refuge for killing by accident
'Without seeing', words from the פסוק about accidental killing

phrases.english: From those liable to exile:
phrases.notes: This picks up רבי יהודה's list from step 24. Now we get the source for the exile part.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Without seeing'
leaves out a blind person. These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַסּוֹמֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: it comes to include a blind person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for בושת in step 26, this continues answering step 25's question for the next item on the list, גלות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads 'בלא ראות' as leaving out a סומא from גלות. רבי מאיר disagrees and reads it as including him.

steps.title: Asking for רבי יהודה's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה reads 'בלא ראות' as leaving out a blind person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי יהודה's reading. This sets up the explanations of both sides that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only told us what each תנא holds. Now the גמרא wants to know how each one gets his reading out of the פסוקים.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling quoted in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי יהודה get the idea that a סומא is left out of גלות from the words 'בלא ראות'?

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the wood-chopping verse would include a blind person
steps.stepSummary: The general פסוק about chopping wood in the forest would have included even a סומא, so the תורה wrote 'בלא ראות' to leave him out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the פסוק says, 'Like one who goes with his friend into the forest to chop wood.' That sounds like it includes even a blind person. So the תורה wrote 'without seeing' to leave him out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה: one פסוק is broad enough to include a blind person, so a second phrase is needed to take him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forest פסוק in דברים describes an accident without any condition about seeing, so on its own it would cover a blind killer too. 'בלא ראות' fits only someone who could have seen and just didn't see this time. That is why רבי יהודה reads it as leaving out a person who can't see at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: He would say to you: 'And one who comes with his friend'
'into the forest to chop wood'
and that would include even a blind person;
so the Merciful One wrote 'without seeing' to leave him out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The broad forest פסוק would include a סומא, so 'בלא ראות' was written to leave him out of גלות.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: two exclusions in a row make an inclusion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר points to two leaving-out phrases, 'בלא ראות' and 'בבלי דעת'. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, together they include a סומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says: the תורה wrote 'without seeing' to leave something out, and it also wrote 'without knowing' to leave something out. That is one leaving-out after another, and a leaving-out after a leaving-out comes only to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי מאיר's opposite view, using the rule that two exclusions in a row actually include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר sees two phrases that each look like they shut out a blind person. Because there are two of them, he applies the rule מיעוט אחר מיעוט, and they cancel out into an inclusion. So a סומא who kills by accident does go to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Without knowing', words from the פסוק about accidental killing
One exclusion after another, which the rule says comes to include

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but in this rule two exclusions in a row do not exclude twice. They add up to an inclusion, so רבי מאיר ends up including the blind person.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir:
the Merciful One wrote 'without seeing' to leave something out,
and the Merciful One wrote 'without knowing' to leave something out;
this makes one leaving-out after another leaving-out,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and a leaving-out after a leaving-out comes only to include.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning of רבי מאיר, after רבי יהודה's reasoning in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בלא ראות' and 'בבלי דעת' are two exclusions, and two exclusions in a row include, so a סומא goes to גלות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule מיעוט אחר מיעוט אין אלא לרבות, a reading tool that the גמרא uses in other places too.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'without knowing' leaves out someone who meant to kill
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that 'בבלי דעת' is not a second exclusion of a סומא. It comes to leave out a מתכוין, someone who meant to kill.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? That phrase 'without knowing' comes to leave out someone who meant to kill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה answers רבי מאיר's argument by giving 'בבלי דעת' a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's argument needs both phrases to be about the blind person. רבי יהודה says 'בבלי דעת' is about something else entirely: a person who meant to kill does not go to גלות. So there is only one exclusion of a סומא, and it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who acted on purpose, who meant to kill
That comes, that is there for

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: 'בלא ראות' leaves out a סומא from גלות, and 'בבלי דעת' leaves out a מתכוין. רבי מאיר: both phrases make a מיעוט אחר מיעוט, so a סומא is included and does go to גלות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי יהודה would answer רבי מאיר's double-exclusion argument.

phrases.english: That phrase 'without knowing'
comes to leave out someone who meant to kill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the מיעוט אחר מיעוט argument of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives one of the two phrases a different purpose, so there is no double exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both 'בלא ראות' and 'בבלי דעת' exclude a סומא, which would make a מיעוט אחר מיעוט that includes him.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בבלי דעת' leaves out a מתכוין, so only 'בלא ראות' excludes a סומא, and he does not go to גלות.

steps.title: Death penalty exemption learned from exile through the word 'killer'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns that a סומא is exempt from מיתות בית דין by a גזירה שוה. The word 'רוצח' appears both by the death penalty and by גלות, so the exemption from גלות carries over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those liable to court death penalties: this is learned from the word 'killer' here and 'killer' there, from those liable to exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה knows that a סומא is also exempt from the court death penalty. It links the death penalty to גלות through the shared word 'רוצח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 showed that 'בלא ראות' leaves a סומא out of גלות. Since the תורה calls both the exiled person and the executed person a 'רוצח', the same rule applies to both. So a סומא who kills on purpose is also not given מיתת בית דין, according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: People who deserve the death penalty given by a court
It comes / it is learned (from another source)
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
People who must go into exile for killing by accident

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'רוצח' is used both for an accidental killer (גלות) and a deliberate killer (death penalty). That shared word is exactly what lets the גזירה שוה connect them.

phrases.english: Those liable to court death penalties –
it is learned from 'killer'–'killer'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:16 (death penalty) and במדבר 35:11 (cities of refuge).

phrases.english: from those liable to exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין אָתְיָא רֹצֵחַ רֹצֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled that a סומא is left out of גלות, the גמרא now extends that exemption to the court death penalty.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סומא is exempt from מיתות בית דין because of the גזירה שוה 'רוצח'–'רוצח' from גלות.

steps.title: Lashes exemption learned from the death penalty through the word 'guilty'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns that a סומא is exempt from מלקות by a second גזירה שוה. The word 'רשע' appears both by מלקות and by the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those liable to lashes: this is learned from the word 'guilty' here and 'guilty' there, from those liable to court death penalties.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the next link in the chain. Just as the death penalty was learned from גלות, now מלקות is learned from the death penalty through the shared word 'רשע'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds directly on step 32: first גלות passed the exemption to מיתות בית דין, and now מיתות בית דין pass it to מלקות. The result is that, for רבי יהודה, a סומא is exempt from all three court punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: People who deserve lashes from the court

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's chain: 'בלא ראות' leaves a סומא out of גלות → 'רוצח' carries this to מיתות בית דין → 'רשע' carries it to מלקות.

phrases.english: Those liable to lashes –
it is learned from 'guilty'–'guilty'
from those liable to court death penalties.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain from step 32, passing the exemption from the death penalty on to lashes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סומא is exempt from מלקות because of the גזירה שוה 'רשע'–'רשע' from מיתות בית דין.

steps.title: Another teaching: a blind person has no shame payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says that a סומא has no בושת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in another ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, a blind person does not have humiliation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new piece of evidence about רבי יהודה's view of a סומא, this time about בושת. This line sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was court punishments. Now it switches to the damage payment for shame, one of the payments of our פרק. The short wording does not yet say exactly how this rule works, so the גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shame / the payment for embarrassing someone

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A blind person does not have humiliation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר סוֹמֵא אֵין לוֹ בּוֹשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the court-punishment derivations, the גמרא brings a different ברייתא of רבי יהודה about a סומא, now dealing with בושת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a סומא has no בושת.
